verdicts.trueWording: a booklet which offers in 96 pages what many books would have needed twice that to do
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Quote appears word for word under 'GAZ3: The Principalities of Glantri / OVERALL', preceded by 'That economy is admirable-'. Byline 'Posted by Lowell Francis', dated Wednesday, April 11, 2012. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: about nine of the major buildings detailed, including the garrison, inn, jeweler, church and general store
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in the paragraph beginning 'The village proper has...'. Hedge recorded: the page says 'about nine of the major buildings detailed', not a flat nine; the count itself is unchanged, so the limb stands. Posted October 7, 2011 by Bryce Lynch.

verdicts.trueWording: decent sized rumor table, as is proper for a home base environment
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim; the full sentence reads 'We also get a decent sized rumor table, as is proper for a home base environment.' The claim renders 'environment' as 'settlement', a faithful paraphrase of the same referent (the village of White Dragon Run as home base).

verdicts.trueWording: The village is a bit ... bland. The occupants all seem to be fine upstanding members of the community
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim. The 'faults' limb is supported by the immediately adjacent 'The village is a bit ... bland' and 'The NPC's, major & minor, just don't seem to have much personality to them.'

verdicts.trueWording: Two sentences: purple stone and crystal, then 'It is ruled by Lord Zavere and Lady Rill.'
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that the key entry is a SINGLE sentence - the A2 CASTLE SHARD entry runs to two sentences, the second naming its rulers
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200), post dated January 14th, 2015. The quoted fragment 'A huge castle made from purple stone' is verbatim in THE KEY at entry A2. But the full entry reads: 'A huge castle made from purple stone, housing a massive crystal with strange magical properties. It is ruled by Lord Zavere and Lady Rill.' - two sentences, not one. Material (stone), colour (purple) and contents (the crystal) are all in the first sentence, so that limb holds; the 'single sentence' limb does not. Neighbouring entries (A1, A3, B5) are likewise one-to-three sentences, so brevity generally is supported - the specific count is not.

verdicts.trueWording: Instead of writing the conclusion, you are writing the clue
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200), dated October 30th, 2020. Quote verbatim in the section headed WRITING THE BOOK; full sentence continues 'which will let the players figure out the conclusion.' All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: it is often useful if the key information is not what the book is primarily about
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in WRITING THE BOOK, opening 'Along the same lines, it is often useful if...'. The claim's 'often' matches the page's 'often useful'. Page adds a qualifying parenthetical ('This is not universally true'), which the claim's 'often' already accommodates.

verdicts.trueWording: Often I achieve this effect by presenting the information in an oblique or mythic manner
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in WRITING THE BOOK. First person 'Often I achieve this effect by...' supports the claim's 'often presents'.

verdicts.trueWording: these handouts more or less serve as an executive summary for a book that doesn't actually exist
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). The supplied quote fragment ends at the curly apostrophe in 'doesn't'; the full page sentence is 'In practice, these handouts more or less serve as an executive summary for a book that doesn't actually exist.' Found in the body paragraph on what lore books are, as cited. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: describe the experience of reading the book ... the physicality of the book itself
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in TIPS & TRICKS: 'As I mentioned before, describe the experience of reading the book.' The 'physical' limb is carried by the same passage ('This can be the physicality of the book itself') and by the earlier 'I will usually also discuss the actual physical interaction with the book.' Note the page's advice is broader than physicality alone - it also covers sequencing and revelation of knowledge - so the claim narrows rather than overstates.

verdicts.trueWording: it is rather difficult to separate what is meant to be scholarship from fancy
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in the first block-indented example handout ('This slim, peculiar volume purports to be "a dream woven from the true and factual accounts of many diverse peoples of the world," but it is rather difficult to separate what is meant to be scholarship from fancy.'), which Alexander presents as his own demonstration text. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: most of the original information about the Yawning Portal is actually contained in the NPC write-up of its proprietor
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200), dated March 31st, 2022. Quote verbatim in THE EARLY DAYS, immediately after the FR1 key line '4. The Yawning Portal (inn) - See Durnan, p. 17', so the FR1 Waterdeep and the North limb and the proprietor (Durnan) limb are both anchored. Page says 'most of the original information', i.e. the earliest material, which is FR1's.

verdicts.trueWording: on the door itself, someone has chalked 'Come Ye Inn'
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in the bulleted list of FRE3 Waterdeep details in THE EARLY DAYS: 'A signboard above the "round door" reads "The Yawning Portal," and "on the door itself, someone has chalked 'Come Ye Inn.'" (sic)'. The 'welcoming visitors' limb is the plain sense of the chalked words themselves (a pun on 'come ye in'); the page quotes them without separately glossing them as a welcome.

verdicts.trueWording: The Portal is a rambling, dingy, blue-tapestried building of smoothly carved pillars and paneling
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in the bulleted list of new details Ruins of Undermountain (1991) adds, in THE EARLY DAYS. The claim drops 'smoothly' from 'smoothly carved pillars'; nothing else differs. All limbs supported.

verdicts.trueWording: Details of the inn itself have been omitted from these pages to allow DMs free rein in customizing this rambling, shady place
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim inside the block quotation from the Ruins of Undermountain boxed set in THE EARLY DAYS, which Alexander introduces as 'which rather hilariously notes:'. All limbs supported.
